question: What is the main goal of food hygiene and safety practices?

options.A: To ensure food is safe and wholesome for consumption
options.B: To make meals taste better and look colorful
options.C: To make cooking faster in large kitchens
options.D: To cut down the cost of buying ingredients

explanation: Food hygiene is all about stopping contamination so the food we eat stays safe and healthy from the farm or market straight to the table!

question: Which type of food hazard includes cleaning chemicals and leftover pesticide sprays?
explanation: You guessed it—chemical hazards involve toxic substances like cleaning agents and farm chemicals that accidentally get into our food supply.

question: Who counts as a 'food handler' in a hospital or school setting?

options.A: Only the head chef in charge of the menu
options.B: The health inspector who visits monthly
options.C: Anyone who touches food, equipment, or utensils during prep or serving
options.D: Patients who eat the food provided

explanation: Anyone who comes into contact with food, plates, or cooking tools is considered a food handler. Safety starts with everyone!

question: Why is the role of a food handler particularly critical in a hospital environment?

options.A: Hospital patients eat more frequently than people outside
options.B: Hospital kitchens prepare larger quantities of food than standard restaurants
options.C: Hospital patients often have weakened immune systems that make them vulnerable to infections
options.D: Hospital food handlers are required to have medical degrees

explanation: Vulnerable patients in healthcare facilities suffer severe complications from foodborne illnesses that healthy people might overcome easily. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h2)

question: Which virus is famous for spreading quickly through food when infected workers don't wash their hands well?
explanation: Norovirus and Hepatitis A are notorious tummy bugs spread by infected food handlers when hands aren't washed properly. Hand hygiene is key!

question: How do most harmful bacteria in food usually get passed around?

options.A: Through skin-to-skin contact between diners and waiters
options.B: By breathing in air in a crowded dining room
options.C: From mosquito bites near kitchen drains
options.D: Through the fecal-oral route via dirty hands, water, or food

explanation: It sounds unpleasant, but germs from waste easily reach food through poor handwashing—this is what we call the fecal-oral route.

question: Which of these personal items must kitchen staff take off before they start working?
explanation: Rings and watches trap dirt and hidden bacteria that are tough to wash away. Taking them off keeps the kitchen truly clean!

question: A kitchen worker comes in with a sudden case of watery diarrhea and a mild fever. What should be done immediately?

options.A: Ask them to wash dishes with hot water instead
options.B: Take them off food handling duties right away
options.C: Tell them to swallow an anti-diarrhea drug and keep working
options.D: Let them work as long as they wear two pairs of gloves

explanation: Any worker showing signs of a tummy bug must be kept away from food immediately to stop germs from spreading to everyone else.

question: What is the name of the temperature zone where bacteria grow and multiply the fastest?
explanation: The 'danger zone' is between 5°C and 60°C. In this warmth, bacteria can double in number in just twenty minutes!

question: Why must raw meat always go on the lowest shelf of the fridge?

options.A: So it is faster for the cooks to grab
options.B: To keep it closest to the fridge cooling fan
options.C: To stop meat juices from dripping onto other foods below
options.D: Because raw meat likes warmer spots than veggies

explanation: Gravity is sneaky! If raw meat drips onto ready-to-eat foods below it, it spreads harmful germs. Always keep raw meat at the bottom.

question: What is the main difference between cleaning and sanitizing?

options.A: Cleaning uses chemicals, while sanitizing uses only plain water
options.B: Cleaning washes away visible dirt, while sanitizing brings germs down to a safe level
options.C: Cleaning kills bacteria, while sanitizing removes grease
options.D: Cleaning is done daily, while sanitizing is done once a year

explanation: Think of cleaning as washing away the physical mess (like grease and crumbs), while sanitizing uses heat or chemicals to knock out invisible germs.

question: Why are rats, mice, and insects so dangerous around a kitchen?

options.A: They make food lose its vitamins too quickly
options.B: They make annoying noises that disturb staff and guests
options.C: They eat too much food and increase restaurant bills
options.D: They carry and spread dangerous germs on their bodies and waste

explanation: Pests carry loads of bacteria, viruses, and parasites. When they crawl over surfaces, they leave behind invisible pathogens that can make people sick.

question: Which government agency is mainly responsible for regulating food safety and standards in Nigeria?

options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)

explanation: NAFDAC is our national watchdog ensuring that food, drugs, and chemicals sold in Nigeria are safe for everyone.

question: Why do food workers in Nigeria need a mandatory medical certificate?

options.A: To prove they are free from infectious diseases before handling food
options.B: To test how well they can cook local dishes
options.C: To help local government offices generate revenue
options.D: To figure out the right salary level for kitchen staff

explanation: Medical checks ensure that kitchen staff aren't carrying hidden infections that could easily spread to the meals they prepare.

question: What is the best way to tell if a food safety training program actually worked?

options.A: Watching to see if workers practice safe habits on the kitchen floor
options.B: Making sure everyone memorized the manual word-for-word
options.C: Calculating how much money was spent on the workshop
options.D: Checking that everyone sat through every minute of the lecture

explanation: Real learning shows in daily habits! True success is when staff actually use what they learned while cooking and cleaning.

question: Why is interactive training better for food workers than just reading a textbook?

options.A: Textbooks are too costly for big restaurant teams
options.B: Reading books is strictly banned in commercial kitchens
options.C: Adults learn and remember better through hands-on practice and real examples
options.D: Practical training means workers don't need health certificates

explanation: We learn best by doing! Hands-on practice helps us understand safety rules better and remember them when it counts.
